Submission

Submission Guidelines

Submission is live

ISORC 2027 submissions will follow IEEE conference formatting requirements. Final page limits and review policies can be found on the official CFP.

Submit via HotCRP IEEE Templates

Formatting

IEEE double-column format

Authors should prepare manuscripts using the standard IEEE conference proceedings template in double-column format. Submissions must be written in English and should present original work that has not been simultaneously submitted elsewhere.

Figures, tables, algorithms, and references must remain readable after PDF generation. Authors should verify fonts, margins, embedded figures, hyperlinks, and accessibility of the generated PDF before submission.

Expected manuscript categories

  • Regular Research Papers: full technical contributions with complete evaluation.
  • Industrial Papers and Practitioner Reports: applied systems, deployments, tools, and lessons learned.
  • Short Papers: focused contributions, early results, or emerging ideas with clear novelty.

Submission Portal

The official HotCRP submission portal is now open for paper submissions.

Open Submission Portal

Important: New account registration required. This is a newly deployed submission system — accounts from previous conferences or other HotCRP installations will not work here. If you have not registered on the ISORC 2027 portal before, select “Create an account” on the portal's sign-in page and complete registration before submitting.

Policies

Use of AI Tools

ISORC 2027 follows IEEE's guidelines and policies on the use of artificial intelligence tools in scholarly submission and peer review. The policy below applies separately to authors and to reviewers.

For Authors

Authors

Tools such as Grammarly or other AI assistants may be used to improve the presentation of a submission. However, authors remain fully responsible for the accuracy of all information presented and for the originality and validity of their contributions.

Authors should follow the applicable IEEE policies regarding the use of AI-generated content. Any use of AI-generated text should be disclosed in the paper's Acknowledgements section, in accordance with IEEE requirements. Where applicable, sections containing AI-generated text should include an appropriate citation to the AI system used.

Authors are responsible for ensuring that the use of AI tools does not compromise the originality, integrity, confidentiality, or accuracy of their submission.

IEEE Guidelines on AI-Generated Text

For Reviewers

Reviewers

ISORC 2027 follows IEEE's policies concerning the use of AI tools during the peer-review process.

In particular, reviewers must not use public AI tools or other external AI systems to process, upload, summarize, analyze, or generate review content based on manuscripts under review. Manuscripts and information contained in them are confidential, and submitting such material to external AI systems may constitute a breach of confidentiality.

Reviewers are expected to evaluate manuscripts personally and independently and remain fully responsible for the content and recommendations of their submitted reviews.

IEEE Submission and Peer-Review Policies
